free_tier.stated: unverified: no free tier, free credit or trial is stated on https://nanite.run/ or https://superhq.ai/; both pages price the hosted sandbox only by component usage drawn down from prepaid credits ('One credit is one US dollar'), with 'No seats, no plans, no minimums'
free_tier.notes: The sign-up pages superhq.ai/signup and nanite.run/signup answered HTTP 404 on 2026-11-25, so no new-user credit could be confirmed either way. The shuru runtime under the sandbox is Apache 2.0 software the user installs and runs on a Mac or Linux ARM64 machine; Nanite is the hosted service and is the offer priced here.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a microVM with a disk and files, not a single object; uploads are written through the filesystem API
per_object_cap.notes: New sandboxes get a 20 GiB disk; no per-file cap is published on the pages read.

retention.stated: unverified: no retention period for sandboxes or checkpoints is stated on the pages read; a sleeping sandbox keeps its disk and files, and when credits run out running sandboxes stop and their disks are kept

egress.terms: $0.15 per GB out: data sent to the internet is billed, data coming in is free; outbound traffic works out of the box

interface_detail: Plain HTTP calls with a bearer key; POST /v1/sandboxes, POST /v1/sandboxes/{name}/exec, PUT /v1/sandboxes/{name}/fs/write, POST /v1/sandboxes/{name}/checkpoint, PUT /v1/sandboxes/{name}/secrets/{key}; interactive sessions use the same routes over a WebSocket. Every endpoint lives under https://api.nanite.run/v1 and takes an API key in the Authorization header.
tooling: curl and any HTTP client; a shell over a WebSocket; the shuru CLI is the open-source runtime the user can install and run on their own Mac or Linux ARM64 machine, listed last and not the hosted offer priced here.
chaining: Prepaid credits draw down per second across sandboxes; a sleeping sandbox costs only its disk, so an agent that parks between messages keeps its files for later calls, and secrets are injected by the proxy only to hosts the user names.

limits.value: 25 concurrent sandboxes per organisation, 100 kept; 4 vCPU, 8 GiB memory and a 20 GiB disk per new sandbox
a sandbox goes to sleep after 30 seconds with nothing running against it; CPU and memory billing stop while asleep

limits_note: Compute is billed per second on actual CPU and memory in use, minimum 0.125 cores in a container is not stated here; arm64 only, x86 binaries are not supported yet, and the service runs in Sydney, Australia for now.
binding_note: No free allowance exists, so the first limit a user meets is the paid prepaid-credit balance and the 25-sandbox concurrency cap; idle sandboxes sleep, so wall-clock runtime is not the binding constraint.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: no public sign-up form was read on 2026-11-25; superhq.ai/signup and nanite.run/signup both answered HTTP 404. An API key is issued by the hosted console, so an email is the nearest kind; whether registration also asks for a card is unverified.

reliability_note: A sandbox sleeps after 30 seconds idle and wakes on the next request with its files intact; when prepaid credits run out, running sandboxes stop and keep their disks until the user tops up.
confidence_note: The prices, sandbox size, concurrency cap, sleep rule and credit terms are quoted from the first-party nanite.run page and the SuperHQ home page read on 2026-11-25; the identity gate and retention period are unverified because the sign-up pages are gone.
